summary:
The trick's order of revealing positions doesn't depend on the numbers at all. So run the trick on the
positions `0..n−1` with a queue (reveal the front, move the next to the back) and hand out the sorted cards in
that order: the k-th revealed position gets the k-th smallest card. O(n log n) for the sort.

question.md:
Repeatedly: reveal the top card, then move the next top card to the bottom. Arrange the deck so the cards come
out in increasing order, and return it top to bottom.

- **Cards are distinct**, so "increasing order" fixes exactly which card is revealed at each turn.
- **The last card** is just revealed; there's nothing to move.
- **Up to 10⁵ cards.**

think.md:
Cards `[5, 2, 9, 7, 1, 4]`. The answer is `[1, 5, 2, 9, 4, 7]`: running the trick on it reveals 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9.

Notice the trick never looks at the numbers: it moves **positions** around in a fixed pattern. Number the deck
positions 0 (top) to 5. Run the trick on the positions: the first position revealed must hold the smallest
card, the second the next smallest, and so on.

"Reveal the front, move the next to the back" is exactly a queue. Alternatively, the trick can be **run in
reverse**: starting from the largest card, put cards back on top, undoing the move each time.

approaches.title: Undo the trick with an array

idea.md: Go through the sorted cards from largest to smallest and rebuild the deck backwards. Undoing one round means: undo 'move the top card to the bottom' (take the bottom card back to the top), then undo 'reveal' (put the card back on top). With a plain array, each move to the front costs O(n).

build: From the largest: if the deck isn't empty, move its last card to the front; then insert the card at the front.

lines.text: The deck being rebuilt, top first.
Cards from largest to smallest: the last card revealed is put back first.

notes.c: The comparator returns the sign without subtracting, so it can't overflow.

lines.text: The forward trick moved the top card to the bottom right after revealing; undo it by taking the bottom card back to the top.
Undo the reveal: this card goes back on top.

notes.c: `memmove` shifts the deck down one slot to make room at the front.

complexity.md: **Time O(n²):** each insertion at the front shifts the whole array. **Space O(n).**

steps.text: Put back 9: then place 9 on top.
Put back 7: first move the bottom card 9 to the top (undoing 'top to bottom'), then place 7 on top.
Put back 5: first move the bottom card 9 to the top (undoing 'top to bottom'), then place 5 on top.
Put back 4: first move the bottom card 7 to the top (undoing 'top to bottom'), then place 4 on top.
Put back 2: first move the bottom card 9 to the top (undoing 'top to bottom'), then place 2 on top.
Put back 1: first move the bottom card 5 to the top (undoing 'top to bottom'), then place 1 on top.

walk.title: Undo the trick from the end. Take cards from largest to smallest; each step reverses one round: move the bottom card back to the top, then put the card back on top.

limits.md: Front insertions make it quadratic: ~10¹⁰ shifts for 10⁵ cards. A deque would fix that, and so does running the trick forwards on positions with a queue.

approaches.title: Deal sorted cards into positions with a queue

idea.md: Queue the positions `0..n−1`. For each card in increasing order: pop the front position and put the card there; then, if positions remain, move the next front position to the back.

build: For each card: assign it to the popped front; rotate one position to the back.

lines.text: A queue of deck positions, top (0) first, and the deck to fill.

notes.java: A plain array works as the queue: `n` positions start in it and at most `n − 1` are re-added, so `2n` slots never run out.
notes.c: A plain array works as the queue: `n` positions start in it and at most `n − 1` are re-added, so `2n` slots never run out.

lines.text: Cards in the order they must be revealed: increasing.
The trick reveals whatever is at the front position now, so the next smallest card must sit there.
Then the next top card goes to the bottom: rotate one position. Skipped after the last card.

complexity.md: **Time O(n log n)** for the sort; the dealing is O(n). **Space O(n).**

steps.text: Reveal position 0: it gets 1. Position 1 goes to the bottom.
Reveal position 2: it gets 2. Position 3 goes to the bottom.
Reveal position 4: it gets 4. Position 5 goes to the bottom.
Reveal position 1: it gets 5. Position 3 goes to the bottom.
Reveal position 5: it gets 7. Position 3 goes to the bottom.

walk.title: Run the trick on the empty positions 0..n−1 with a queue. The position revealed at each turn receives the next smallest card.

takeaways.md:
- If a process moves **positions** in a fixed pattern regardless of values, simulate it on indices and then
  assign values.
- Any shuffle can also be undone step by step in reverse; use a deque so front operations are O(1).
- "Take from the front, put at the back" = queue.
